summary: A red-brick light and keeper's house on a limestone bluff guarding the Sturgeon Bay canal entrance on Green Bay; the last manned light on the Great Lakes, automated in 1983.

access.note: Coast Guard property; grounds open only on organised open days.

events.note: Congress appropriated $12,000 for the light (HAER: 3 March 1881)
Fog bell struck by machinery, 1 July 1892
Lens and rotating mechanism replaced with apparatus from Passage Island
Assistant keeper Minnie Cochems died at the station 17 August
Fog signal automated with electric diaphragm horns; bell tower made a radio room
Last Great Lakes light to be automated
Fresnel lens removed 21 October and replaced with a 300 mm acrylic optic; lens to Door County Maritime Museum

notes_for_editor: Sources are few: HAER inventory, Pepper, Lighthousefriends, USLHS roster, three Light-House Board report passages. Pepper's text has dropped digits in the appropriation date and the construction-year (reads 'March 31, 188' and 'May 14') so the story does not give those. Pepper writes 'August 30, 1899' for the $100 land appropriation; the Board report says the act was approved 30 August 1890 and the story follows the report. Lens order (4th vs 5th) is disputed and stated as such. Focal plane 61 ft (HAER) vs 60 ft (Pepper). Roster: LHF gives Delmar Wilson 1969-1970, USLHS 1967-1970; Pepper's keeper list link (Phyllis Tag) not read. William Cochems's 1953 death comes from LHF only. The 1892 bell date was read from OCR of the 1893 report (fiscal year ended 30 June 1893; scan page 18, printed page uncertain). Peter Sherwood and condemnation story rests on Lighthousefriends alone. Checker: roster dates of Cochems as first assistant 1894 follow Pepper; Lighthousefriends says May 1895. Radio room date differs between Pepper (1940), HAER (addition 1935) and Lighthousefriends (broadcasts from 1937); stated in text.
